subtype: Approach: makes a public promise to keep on track [Action]
passage: Anjali, come, I will tell you about the time Dorje bragged. I was fifteen, and I had started a coding tutorial three times and quit three times. One Sunday, half joking, I typed into our class group: "I will finish the whole coding tutorial in thirty days." Thumbs-ups came back, and one boy wrote, "Let's see." My ears went hot. I did not want to look foolish. So I took a pencil and drew a chart on the door: one hour every evening after dinner, seven to eight. On the lazy days, the chart and the group were both staring at me. I finished on day twenty-nine. I still think about how the promise pushed me on the tired days.

qa.q: How many days did Dorje promise?
How did Dorje feel when the boy wrote "Let's see"?
qa.a: Dorje felt embarrassed and did not want to look foolish.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story helped Dorje keep the promise?
qa.a: Drawing a chart for one hour every evening, seven to eight, turned the promise into a daily routine.

qa.q: How might the classmate who wrote "Let's see" have viewed the promise?
qa.a: The classmate might have doubted it, since it was a big claim, and may have felt impressed when it was finished.

grounding: Shows a teenager promising the class group to finish a coding tutorial and setting a daily hour so as not to look foolish.

subtype: Approach: makes a public promise to keep on track [Action]
passage: Divyansh typed it into his class group before he could chicken out: "I'm finishing the web design tutorial in 30 days. You can check." Twelve thumbs came back, and one "sure bro 😏". That stung. Now he had to do it. The problem was the laptop: his sister Deepika needed it every evening for her college work, and the power went off at least twice a week. So he set a rule. One hour every morning, six to seven, before anyone else woke up. He charged the laptop the night before in case of cuts, and kept a notebook to tick each day. On day nine the power went at six-twenty; he read the lesson notes on his phone instead. On day thirty he posted a link to his first web page.

qa.q: What time did Divyansh set for his daily hour?
qa.a: One hour every morning, six to seven.

qa.q: Why did the 'sure bro' reply sting Divyansh?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed that someone doubted him, and didn't want to look foolish in front of the class.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do if mornings stop working for him?
qa.a: Find another fixed hour when the laptop is free, and keep ticking the notebook so the promise stays visible.

qa.q: How might Deepika see Divyansh's early mornings?
qa.a: She keeps her evenings with the laptop and might be quietly impressed that he got up at six every day.

grounding: A teen promises his class group he will finish a coding tutorial in a month and sets a daily hour so as not to look foolish.

subtype: Approach: makes a public promise to keep on track [Action]
passage: In the school coding club group, Anirban posted a challenge: "Who can build a small game in a month?" Varun, who usually lurked, surprised himself by replying, "Me. By the 30th. Watch." Anirban pinned the message. Walking home past the vegetable market, Varun's stomach turned. Now everyone would see if he quit. That night he stuck a paper calendar above his desk in the flat and wrote: 7 to 8 pm, game tutorial, every day. He told his mother not to call him for dinner before eight. Some nights he did only one tiny lesson. He crossed off every day anyway. On the 28th he shared a jumpy little frog game in the club group. Anirban replied first: "Told you you'd do it."

qa.q: What did Anirban pin in the group?
How did Varun feel walking home past the vegetable market?
qa.a: He felt nervous, his stomach turning, because now everyone would see if he quit.

qa.q: Which small step helped Varun keep the promise?
qa.a: Setting a fixed hour, 7 to 8 pm, and crossing off each day on a calendar, even when he did only one tiny lesson.

qa.q: How does Anirban see Varun's promise?
qa.a: Anirban seems encouraging from the start, pinning the message and cheering when the game is shared.

grounding: A teen tells his coding club group he'll finish a game tutorial in a month and sets a daily hour so as not to look foolish.
